Params: Vertigo hits you before reality does.
The ground trembles. The water trembles. Even the "sky" trembles...
After standing frozen for a few seconds, you finally open your eyes just enough to "see" what lies ahead of you.
Reality and illusion overlap, fighting for dominance in your vision.
A writhing mass of bionic Corrupted... or rather, a fusion of Corrupted.
Dead, living, fragmented... Everything melds together around "Carcosa" to form a unified entity.
Massive deep-sea creatures have claimed the machine as their nest, as tentacles grow along every crevice, unfurling through the air like wings.
And the Punishing Virus binds them all together.
The CPF is the weapon that has kept Carcosa from spreading further, but it is on the verge of collapse.
Nearly half the electronic components have gone dark after the prolonged infection. The filter struggles to hold on, as toxic fog seeps out where it can no longer contain the virus.
A prominent crystalline structure sits at the peak of the tower. Carcosa's tentacles instinctively reach for it, only to recoil in pain.
That crystalline structure... that's the amplifier Kiki's after.
So that's how the original base managed to set up a CPF. They housed the amplifier that keeps the city's projection running in the filter.
In reality, Xoth lies in ruins, its people controlled by the "projection" and reduced to little more than living corpses.
The Choir members prostrate themselves in worship, their bodies and souls withered like dry kindling.
The Wanderers' Lodge is nothing but a crumbling wall, its occupants on the verge of falling down it.
Carcosa looms above, surveying its mortal pasture, its gaze drifting along with the movement of the crowds.
That's enough. Let's end the connection.
One more look! Let me find the exit! Just a little longer!
There is only one escape route: the elevator beneath the base. It goes through Carcosa's "body," providing a path to the exit protected by the CPF.
Through your terminal, you can see text data stream endlessly into the mainframe. That must be how the Choir "feeds" Carcosa.
So that's why everyone who left lost their memories. The Choir's been harvesting those memories to feed Carcosa.
Their memories come from Carcosa's Punishing Virus!
The Choir... or at least that Administrator has known what this so-called god is all along!
But Karenina and you both understand that Xoth would fully become a Corrupted zone without the CPF.
When that happens, Carcosa won't just require data anymore. It will consume every living thing still acting out the script.
Overexposed white spots and scan lines creep into the edges of your vision, like old film burning away.
Karenina nods and closes her eyes. You steady her as her strength gives out.
Her turbulent M.I.N.D. gradually calms down. When she opens her eyes again, you both see the decadent, beautiful metropolis once more.
Relief washes over you. You gasp for air, as if you have just surfaced from a deep dive.
Only after confirming everything is stable do you finally disconnect.
I'd rather blow everything up than sit around watching things go south.
Don't shut off your visual module again.
And stop putting yourself in danger like that.
Commandant, I've got a crazy idea.
You give her an affirming look.
Why don't we... attend that competition, and...
Kill Carcosa during the Songstress Trial.
End this dream of the binary star.
The breeding ground for evil has reached its limit. If left unchecked, the waters inside and outside the base will all fall to the Red Tide soon enough.
I did pretty good this time, didn't I?
You did great, Karenina. Good job!
The final mission assigned to you by the system is to find an appropriate outfit for the concert.
Ever since entering the Master Tailor's mirror mansion, all you can hear is the constant back-and-forth of refusals and exclamations.
The only ones dashing between the fitting rooms and clothing racks are Deerbear and Huhunina.
While Kiki is away on a <color=#ff4e4eff>special mission</color>, they've been entrusted to Karenina's care.
Try this one, Karenina. Trust me on this.
You'd have to tie me up to get me into something covered in pink bows. Absolutely not!
That's coral pink. If you can't tell the difference, you should trust the professional!
What about this one then? It's a brand new design, themed after the Jade Rabbit. I'm going to lose it if you don't like this either.
There's way too many pompoms on this thing! And what's this supposed to be? Ears?! And what about this?!
Don't even think about it! Nobody in their right mind would wear this outside... or inside!
After what sounds like an all-out brawl, the exhausted Master Tailor finally emerges from the fitting room, flashing an OK sign.
But Karenina remains holed up in the fitting room, refusing to come out no matter how many times she is called.
She has been in there by herself for 40 minutes now.
If she does not come out soon, she will go on tonight's performance without any rehearsal.
I'm warning you! Don't you dare laugh! Not even secretly!
No, that's not good enough! Promise me again, Commandant, and mean it this time!
And one more thing! You better compliment me when I come out! No criticisms allowed!
What could this coating possibly look like?
That's not true at all! It's gaudy, overdone... I look like a freaking Christmas tree!
Then I'll just stay here with you until nightfall.
It's fine if we push back the rehearsal a bit.
We've already had our perfect performance together.
Besides, this isn't a competition anyway.
But just because this is a fake performance... doesn't mean I shouldn't treat it professionally.
Karenina sweeps the curtain aside and strides out with confidence.
Even though you have prepared yourself, the sight before you is still absolutely captivating.
The fishnet stockings, patent ankle boots, excessive metallic accessories... It is a style Karenina would never choose normally.
But somehow, it suits her perfectly, as if it is drawing out a hidden side of her personality.
Karenina looks absolutely striking. The moment she hits the stage, she will certainly set the crowd on fire, like opening a bottle of shaken soda.
Karenina strikes her signature pose, placing her hands on her hips before leaning in close and pulling a face, sticking her tongue out playfully.
So, what do you think of my outfit, Commandant?
Karenina drops the act and stares at you intently for a moment, until she finally breaks into laughter.
I mean the coating looks adorable.
No, wait... I mean you look adorable, Karenina.
I mean... you do, normally or right now.
You are always... Well, you get what I'm saying.
Heh heh, I know, I know!
It's not the kind of style I'd normally go for, but trying something new once in a while is pretty fun.
Getting into the spirit, Karenina grabs an electric guitar and sways her shoulders to the rhythm as she hums a melody. You cannot help but play along with her antics.
The whole display was pretty silly, as if you were a couple of kids instead of grown adults.
At that thought, you both dissolve into shared laughter.
Until the system notification in your vision flickers to the next item.
Oh crap, we're gonna be late, Commandant! Let's get moving!
Karenina grabs your hand and the electric guitar, and you dash toward your destination without a care in the world.
You spend most of your time backstage after that. You feel a bit rusty with the rhythm at first, but your muscle memory comes flooding back after you get the hang of it.

Your fingers are wrapped in bracelets and bandages from playing too hard. As time slips by, you lose yourself in the creative process, familiarizing yourself with the score while experimenting with new directions.
Practice consumes your every thought. Whenever a new detail comes to mind, you stop immediately to share it with Karenina.

The two of you argue endlessly over a particular melody. What started as practice for the mission has evolved into a desire to create the perfect piece, and this desire now overshadows everything else.
You are so focused that you have managed to ignore the system countdown. Only the gradually darkening sky reminds you that the performance draws near.
When someone opens the door to tell you it is time to go onstage, you cannot help but feel a pang of regret.
This uninterrupted time together is far too short in the end.
But when Karenina takes her place backstage, she cannot help but sneak a peek at the crowd below. Flickering light strips have formed a glittering pathway of stars.
Ahhh! What's going on, Commandant?! I can't hear my in-ear monitors... All I can hear is my own heartbeat.
To calm herself down as quickly as possible, Karenina starts taking deep breaths through her mouth.
You reach out and cover her ears. In the complete darkness, your heartbeats gradually synchronize.
Imagine it's just the two of us performing.
With one final deep breath, Karenina finally calms down.
As you lower your hand, she catches it and holds it tight.
Commandant... thanks for staying by my side this whole time.
Her voice is so soft, you almost mistake it for your imagination.
But the composure on her face quietly confirms it all.
You wait in silence for the final moment to arrive, listening to the clamor of the crowd. Your fingers gradually intertwine, then quietly pull apart.
Songstress Trial begins in 01 second... Performance begins.
The spotlight catches Karenina as she descends, cradling her in moonlight.
Before the lights find you, you slip back into the shadows, only to be caught by a few stagehands and escorted to a seat.
Karenina moves, but her mind is blank. Her body runs on autopilot, driven purely by muscle memory.
It is as if the entire city has gathered here. Jellyfish, silverfish, and bioluminescent creatures have become living sources of light.
She steps to the center of the stage, grips the microphone, and closes her eyes.
The world falls silent, waiting until she's ready for the moment...
...When the bottle of soda bursts forth and weaves together sweetness and energy.
Her first note trembles slightly. Karenina grips the microphone tighter, and her voice gradually steadies.
Her shoulders loosen, and she begins to move with the music, her body flowing freely.
Through the amplifiers, every inflection and rise in her voice is captured and magnified with perfect clarity.
Karenina struggles to focus, searching the crowd for the one she longs to see. But you have been pushed into an audience of thousands, and your presence is indiscernible.
As the first chorus kicks in, Karenina stretches out her hand, pointing at you.
The eyes never lie. All her senses sharpen into instinct, locking onto what matters most instantly.
The crowd's cheers surge with excitement. Karenina's voice is not perfect, but it is the sound of youth itself.
The raw, unpolished voice is breathing new life into Xoth, like mint, like ice, like sparks.
Fireworks and confetti are launched into the air. Karenina becomes a silhouette, drawing the gaze of everyone present.
She stops worrying about whether her performance is flawless. She doesn't care about beating anyone anymore.
So what if your story feels like something out of a third-rate cliche movie?
So what if the performance isn't perfect? So what if there are shaky notes, awkward breaths, and missed beats?
This is your summer. This is your irreplaceable rhythm!
Drenched in sweat, she sways to the rhythm with everyone else, singing her heart out.
As the drawn-out electronic tone fades to silence, the song ends. Karenina gasps for breath, lights switching off around her one by one.
Whatever happens, we pulled it off!
I was one with the music... I felt every single beat... I have no regrets.
About ten seconds later, the crowd erupts in deafening cheers.
The crowd keeps chanting her name, and a name is the simplest declaration in the world.
The performance was a smashing success!
But when the lights come back up and you move to greet Karenina, the mic and electric guitar lie abandoned on an empty stage.
Confetti drifts down like snow. The crowd falls silent, as if someone has hit the mute button.
The number of steps ahead does not register with you. The path to the stage just feels endless.
You push through the crowd and head toward backstage, searching frantically, but there is no trace of Karenina anywhere.
You trip on a cable, causing several stage lights to fall, and an anchor pendant tumbles out.
Fear grips your stomach like tentacles. This is just like that ominous dream.
Your fists clenched, you try to steady your racing heartbeat. Then, slumped on the floor, you remember this is where you and Karenina locked eyes just moments ago.
The waves push the stage upward, while the props and decorations peel away. The stage is transforming into an aircraft carrier before your eyes.
Gale winds whip up from all sides, as a war horn echoes from the depths below.
A faint tremor travels up from the ground, as if a hunting army is drawing closer.
Waves and mist interweave and merge. Within the deep blue-black expanse, the curtain rises to reveal cold stars filling the sky.
Eyes more terrible than the abyss rise from the water. Carcosa has awakened.
The Choir members spread their arms wide and begin their song: a grating, hissing cacophony so hoarse and jarring it sounds like the belly-rumbling of serpents.
The stage warps and transforms into an altar. Stone steps materialize before you, leading up to the platform.
Through the murky deluge pouring from the sky, Karenina ascends the steps, surrounded by the throng.
We give thanks to the sea below, to the stars above, to the dark moon and the tide...
Today, we offer unto Carcosa once more... a Songstress!
Her Song of True Love has awakened Carcosa, and Xoth shall grant her the future of civilization in return.
Let the Songstress and Carcosa guide the lost kin and chart our voyage to the stars!
Depart! Depart! Bathe in the boundless blessings!
You shove through the crowd, but shadowy hands seep out from both sides, blocking your way to their "sacrifice."
No matter how hard you struggle, she remains just out of reach.
The storm rages harder. Rain pelts your body like gunfire, and your eyelids are sealed shut by the warm, murky torrent.
The only thing you can cling to is the white, pure figure.
Is this really where it ends? No... You won't stop here.
While you race toward her, Karenina's consciousness is present in another realm.
Karenina, what's going through your head?
You need to finalize the construction plan for the Sky Base's lower hull by the end of the month.
Otherwise, your teacher is going to be furious. Trust me, you don't want to see him angry.
Sunlight streams into the laboratory. Outside the window, cherry blossoms drift down like a woven tapestry.
On the windowsill sits a potted plant with fresh sprouts. Spring is here, and the plant is growing.
Hmph, piece of cake. Besides, Grandpa could never stay mad at me.
Her comms buzzes, but Karenina instinctively hides it in her sleeve, knowing who it is that's calling her.
Don't say I didn't warn you if Lucia's team submits their report early.
And make sure you're back before curfew. Don't make your Grandpa wait for you.
I know, I know! Alright, I'll hand in the report and be home on time.
Karenina rushes out the door, only to collide with Bianca, who is coming in from the other side. She stumbles, but Bianca catches her before she falls.
Meanwhile, Teddy happens to pass by and watches the whole scene unfold with obvious amusement.
Karenina, you haven't been to the reading group in ages. Keep this up and you'll lose credits for your elective.
Someone hacked my account and signed me up for that! I never agreed to it.
That "someone" flashes a smug grin before turning around and walking away, her pink twin-tails swaying behind her.
Karenina does not chase after her, because someone is waiting at the theater.
For some reason, the moment she sees you, the world around her ripples like water.
The white light from the distortion looks like sunlight filtering through film.
It won't take long. Just hold on until she enters the coffin.
This place was custom-built from her own fantasies. She looks happy, doesn't she?
Yeah. The kind of happiness she never got in the real world.
I'm fine. Movie's about to start, and I'm not missing the opening this time.
Karenina spots the giant tub of popcorn and drinks in your arms.
She must admit she craves this kind of happiness.
Tickets checked, 3D glasses claimed, seats found... A few ads are all that is left before a 130-minute romance movie.
Commandant, what kind of movie openings do you like best?
"Karenina, what did you just call me?"
An explosion resounds through the theater. Karenina watches as the figure before her burns like paper.
It turns into ash. Code. Symbols.
No, I wasn't calling you... I was calling the real commandant. The one outside.
You're not wearing the tracker. Your eyes, your voice, the way you speak... it's all just mimicry. You're not my commandant.
Karenina grabs a handful of popcorn and tosses it in her mouth with a hint of regret. It is sweet, just as she thought.
With that done, Karenina brushes off her jacket and adjusts her cap before standing.
She steps over the burnt remains, an electric guitar somehow already in hand, and strides toward the screen with purpose.
Fool others if you want, but you shouldn't have tried to fool me.
Sigh, if only this were real. I wish I could catch a movie with the commandant in the real world.
With everything she's got, Karenina grabs the guitar by the neck and swings it down with all her strength without reservation, like always.
Once. Twice. Again. Until the guitar splinters, shards flying up and cutting her face.
When the guitar snaps clean in two, a white light suddenly bleeds through from behind the screen. That sliver of a way out finally makes her stop.
Karenina reaches out and touches the crack. The entire world crumbles to dust, starting from her fingertips.
Watching the dust scatter and drift away, she points a finger gun toward it, then pulls her hand back and blows away imaginary gunsmoke.
A real sound... one that can pierce through illusions.
It comes from the <phonetic=tracker>anchor pendant</phonetic> outside, accompanied by heartbeats, each stronger than the last.
Mm... It was nice, but a story is still just a story.
Karenina steps out of the crumbling fantasy and runs toward you, joy written all over her face.
Just hold on a little longer. I'm coming for you right now. Running, actually.
It is an anchor Karenina set for herself.
